macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Nvidia-led rally sends U.S. stocks sharply higher
items.summary: The Dow rose 3.01%, the S&P 500 gained 4.73%, and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 6.51% on Nov. 23, marking the major indexes’ strongest rebound in months. Nvidia surged about 31%–33% after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, adding roughly $900 billion to its market value.[1][3][5]

items.title: Fed remains a central market risk ahead of December decision
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said inflation is about 3.5%, well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target, while describing the labor market as solid. Markets continued to price a high probability of a quarter-point rate increase at the Fed’s December meeting.[1][8]
items.source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York / Barron’s

items.title: Semiconductor shares extend Nvidia-driven rebound
items.summary: Micron rose about 19% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained roughly 13% as investors rotated back into high-growth technology stocks following the Nvidia leadership announcement.[1]

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Zscaler
items.summary: CrowdStrike announced an agreement to buy cybersecurity rival Zscaler in a deal valued at about $43.9 billion, adding a major technology-sector corporate transaction to the day’s market activity.[5]

items.title: Dollar and gold rise as risk sentiment improves
items.summary: The dollar index moved above 104 for the first time since April 2025, while gold rebounded more than 4% and Treasury yields edged lower as markets recovered from the prior week’s sharp sell-off.[2]

items.title: Investors await global flash PMI data
items.summary: November flash purchasing-managers surveys for the United States, eurozone, and United Kingdom were highlighted as key upcoming indicators for economic momentum and the outlook for further central-bank rate increases.[4][7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $61,000 after sharp selloff
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered above $61,000 after falling near $55,000 and triggering roughly $1.8 billion in liquidations. Ethereum also rose about 2% to above $1,715, while Bitcoin remained down more than 20% for the month.

items.title: Chainflip hack losses rise to about $12 million
items.summary: Cross-chain protocol Chainflip reported that losses from an exploit had grown to approximately $12 million, including 122.86 BTC and 520.22 ETH. The protocol offered the attacker a 10% bounty to return the remaining funds.

items.title: UK formalizes regulated stablecoin framework
items.summary: The UK enacted amendments to its cryptoasset regime that classify qualifying stablecoin issuance as a regulated activity and require issuers to establish a UK presence.

items.title: South Korea prepares broader crypto legislation
items.summary: South Korea is expected to publish a draft comprehensive cryptocurrency legal framework, alongside tighter anti-money-laundering rules focused on overseas exchanges and wallet transfers.

items.title: Monad token unlock scheduled for November 24
items.summary: Monad is set to release approximately 16.6 billion MON tokens, equivalent to about 32.37% of its circulating supply and valued near $219 million, potentially increasing selling pressure.

items.title: CFTC approves blockchain-based derivatives exchange
items.summary: The CFTC approved a blockchain-based derivatives exchange as U.S. regulators continued developing rules for on-chain market infrastructure and crypto trading platforms.

items.title: Tokenized stocks on Base surpass $1 billion in weekly volume
items.summary: Tokenized stock trading on Base, Coinbase’s Ethereum layer-2 network, exceeded $1 billion in weekly volume less than three months after launch.

items.title: MoonPay applies for U.S. national bank charter
items.summary: Crypto payments company MoonPay reportedly applied for a U.S. national bank charter, signaling plans to expand its regulated financial-services footprint.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA VI launch drives major industry headlines
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly surpassed 32.5 million copies sold by the end of its first day, including preorders, setting a record for initial revenue among entertainment products. The game launched on November 19, 2026, and continues to dominate gaming coverage.[1]

items.title: GTA VI physical release fuels digital-only debate
items.summary: Retail copies of GTA VI reportedly include download codes rather than game discs, prompting criticism from GameStop’s chief executive and renewed debate over the future of physical game distribution.[2]

items.title: BioWare reportedly closes after final working day
items.summary: BioWare’s reported closure was identified as one of the weekend’s most significant industry developments, marking another major studio disruption amid continuing restructuring across the games business.[1]

items.title: 007 First Light wins 2026 TIGA Game of the Year
items.summary: IO Interactive’s 007 First Light received Game of the Year at the 2026 TIGA Games Industry Awards.[8]

items.title: This week’s notable game releases include Gothic 3 Classic
items.summary: Gothic 3 Classic is scheduled for release on November 24, while Stellaris: Willpower launched on November 23. The release calendar is relatively quiet as publishers avoid competing directly with GTA VI.[7]
